items.bold: CENTCOM BRIEFED TRUMP. Admiral Cooper: 42 vessels redirected, 41 tankers (69M bbl, $6B) Iran cannot sell.
items.text: NBC News (4 hours ago) and CBS News confirmed: Admiral Brad Cooper, commander of US Central Command, briefed Trump and his senior national security team at the White House Thursday on options for the way ahead in Hormuz. In a separate statement on X, Cooper said the US had redirected 42 vessels attempting to violate the blockade. He also confirmed 41 tankers with 69 million barrels of oil — worth more than $6 billion — "that the Iranian regime can't sell." Cooper: "The blockade is highly effective and US forces remain fully committed to total enforcement." Trump told reporters Thursday: "The power of the blockade is incredible. They're not getting any money from oil, and hopefully it can be worked out very soon." Trump also told energy industry executives this week the blockade would continue "for months if needed."

items.bold: BRENT CLOSED $114.01 — pulled back from $126 intraday. Trump discounted resuming bombing.
items.text: CNBC (7 hours ago) confirmed: Brent crude fell more than 3% to close at $114.01 after surging to a wartime high of $126 earlier in the session. WTI slipped more than 1% to $105.07. The partial pullback came after Trump appeared to discount — though not rule out — resuming bombing Iran. Trump: "I don't know that we need it. We might need it." Markets partially priced out the immediate strike risk. Goldman Sachs estimates exports through Hormuz have fallen to just 4% of normal levels. CNBC (ING commodities strategist Warren Patterson): "The oil market has moved from over-optimism to the reality of the supply disruption we are seeing in the Persian Gulf. The longer this disruption persists, the less the market can rely on inventory, and the greater the need for further demand destruction." Both Brent and WTI are up around 60% since the war began February 28.

items.bold: MOJTABA KHAMENEI — first public signal — vowed to protect Iran's NUCLEAR AND MISSILE capabilities as "national assets."
items.text: NBC News (4 hours ago) confirmed: Iran's new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei vowed in a message Thursday that the Islamic Republic would protect its "nuclear and missile capabilities" as national assets. This is the FIRST confirmed public communication from Mojtaba Khamenei since he became Supreme Leader — his first public signal of where the red lines are. The message is unambiguous: nuclear and missile programmes are non-negotiable for Iran's new Supreme Leader. This directly contradicts Trump's stated condition for ending the blockade (no nuclear weapons capability). The gap between Iran's Supreme Leader's red line (protect nuclear) and Trump's red line (no nuclear) is now explicitly confirmed at the highest level. It makes a near-term deal structurally very difficult.

items.bold: Sen. MURKOWSKI to introduce AUMF May 11. HEGSETH: 60-day war clock "pauses" during ceasefire.
items.text: CNN live blog (1 hour ago) confirmed: GOP Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) announced Thursday she plans to introduce an Authorization for Use of Military Force (AUMF) measure when the Senate returns from recess the week of May 11 — if the White House does not present a "credible plan." Murkowski (Senate floor): "I do not accept that we should engage in open-ended military action without clear direction or accountability. Congress has a role." Defense Secretary Hegseth testified in the Senate that the 60-day war powers clock "pauses" during a ceasefire. "We are in a ceasefire right now, which our understanding means the 60-day clock pauses." Murkowski: "I do not believe that statute would support that." Congressional pressure is now building on the Trump administration. The AUMF deadline of May 11 is the next political pressure point for the war.

items.bold: LEBANON: IDF soldier killed in Hezbollah drone. 14 killed in Nabatieh Israeli strikes. Ceasefire over in practice.
items.text: CNN (1 hour ago) and CBS News confirmed: An Israeli soldier was killed in a Hezbollah drone strike in southern Lebanon Thursday — IDF confirmed. Lebanon's Health Ministry said Israeli strikes across several towns in the Nabatieh district killed at least 14 people. CNN: "Communities in Lebanon are gripped by 'deep fear and uncertainty,' one relief worker in the country told CNN, as the Israeli military launched another wave of lethal strikes on the south." The Lebanon ceasefire is effectively over in practice — both sides are striking and taking casualties despite the formal extension. Iran has repeatedly said it will not agree to any deal that does not also halt Israel's war in Lebanon. The Lebanon escalation is the structural block on any comprehensive US-Iran deal.

items.bold: INDIA: Desh Garima Mumbai photo (Reuters). Brent $114 (eased). OMC hike Rs 9-12/L still imminent.
items.text: Reuters published a significant photograph Thursday: an Indian-flagged tanker, the Desh Garima, photographed unloading crude oil at an offloading terminal in Mumbai "after transiting the Strait of Hormuz, amid supply disruptions linked to the US-Israeli war with Iran." This confirms some India-bound crude is still moving through the Hormuz corridor via coordinated passage — likely using Iran's north-of-Larak-Island toll channel. For India: (1) Brent settled at $114 (down from $126 intraday) — slight market relief, but still 80% above pre-war. (2) OMC hike Rs 9-12/L remains imminent — Brent $114 still far above the OMC break-even. (3) Rupee at Rs 95 — RBI intervention expected. (4) Mojtaba Khamenei's nuclear red line makes a deal structurally harder. (5) Goldman Sachs: exports at 4% of normal — structural tightness for months. India's kharif fertiliser emergency remains: $1M+/ship Hormuz toll makes Gulf fertiliser imports commercially impossible.

military.t: CENTCOM Briefed Trump. 42 Vessels Redirected. 41 Tankers ($6B) Iran Cannot Sell. "Highly Effective."
military.d: NBC News and CBS News confirmed: Admiral Brad Cooper (CENTCOM commander) briefed Trump and senior NSC at the White House Thursday on options for the way ahead in Hormuz and Iran. Cooper separately confirmed on X: the US has redirected 42 vessels attempting to violate the blockade. Additionally, there are 41 tankers holding 69 million barrels of oil — worth more than $6 billion — "that the Iranian regime can't sell." Cooper: "The blockade is highly effective and US forces remain fully committed to total enforcement." Trump to reporters Thursday: "The power of the blockade is incredible. They're not getting any money from oil." Trump told energy industry executives this week the blockade would continue "for months if needed." After the briefing, Trump appeared to discount (but not rule out) resuming bombing: "I don't know that we need it. We might need it."

military.t: MOJTABA KHAMENEI — First Public Signal: Vowed to Protect Nuclear and Missile Capabilities.

The message is structurally significant: Iran's Supreme Leader — who must sign off on any deal — has explicitly said nuclear and missile programmes cannot be touched. Trump's condition for ending the blockade is exactly the opposite: no nuclear capability. The Mojtaba nuclear red line vs Trump's nuclear red line is now explicitly confirmed at the highest level of both governments. This is the structural deadlock that makes a near-term comprehensive deal very difficult.

assessment.body:
Friday 8 AM IST. Day 63. The war's dynamics clarified overnight.

THE CENTCOM BRIEFING — WHAT COOPER CONFIRMED
• 42 vessels redirected attempting to violate the blockade
• 41 tankers with 69 million barrels of oil — worth $6 billion — Iran cannot sell
• "The blockade is highly effective and US forces remain fully committed to total enforcement"
• Trump to energy executives: blockade will continue "for months if needed"
• Trump Thursday: appeared to discount bombing — "I don't know that we need it"
• But did NOT rule it out: "We might need it"

MOJTABA'S RED LINE — THE KEY STRATEGIC SIGNAL
• Mojtaba Khamenei's FIRST confirmed public communication since becoming Supreme Leader
• Vowed to protect Iran's "nuclear and missile capabilities" as national assets
• This is Iran's Supreme Leader setting his opening red lines explicitly
• Directly contradicts Trump's condition: no nuclear capability
• The structural deadlock is now confirmed at the highest level of both governments
• Near-term comprehensive deal: structurally very difficult

BRENT PULLED BACK — BUT STAYS ELEVATED
• Closed at $114.01 after hitting $126 wartime high
• Goldman Sachs: Hormuz exports at just 4% of normal
• 41 tankers ($6B) Iran cannot sell — economic noose tightening
• Even if deal today: $10-20 immediate drop, then Brent $80-90 (structural bottlenecks)
• Both Brent and WTI up ~60% since February 28

THE CONGRESSIONAL PRESSURE
• GOP Sen. Murkowski: AUMF measure coming May 11 if no WH credible plan
• Hegseth: 60-day clock "pauses" during ceasefire (disputed by senators)
• Congress beginning to assert war powers authority
• May 11 = the next political deadline

INDIA AT DAY 63
• Desh Garima photographed unloading in Mumbai after Hormuz transit (Reuters)
• Confirms India-bound crude still moving via coordinated toll channel
• Brent $114 = OMC hike Rs 9-12/L still imminent
• Rupee at Rs 95 — RBI intervention expected
• Kharif fertiliser: Gulf sourcing at $1M+/ship toll remains commercially impossible
• Goldman Sachs 4% flow = structural tightness for months regardless of deal

VERDICT: Day 63 brings partial clarity. The CENTCOM briefing confirmed the blockade's economic effectiveness ($6 billion in Iranian oil going nowhere). Mojtaba Khamenei's first public signal confirmed the nuclear impasse is structural — not just a negotiating position. The Desh Garima photo confirmed India is using coordinated channels to keep some crude flowing. And Murkowski's AUMF threat confirmed Congress is preparing to assert itself if Trump has no plan by May 11. The war is in its most economically effective phase — and its most diplomatically frozen.
